Subject: Question on jurisdiction fallback & SCCs in draft MSA/Order Form

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team is reviewing the DPA and SCCs but flagged two items we need clarified before we can proceed:

1) Jurisdiction fallback — the current export-control clause references a Redwood-hosting fallback that isn't circularly defined. If the EU SCCs are triggered and a hosting fallback is invoked, can you confirm the operational path (i.e., will data move to a specific region or be processed via a dedicated enclave)?

2) Subprocessor routing and export controls — we need a short summary (one page) that maps the subprocessor categories to the hosting regions and any KMS/evidence requirements for cross-border transfers.

We'd like to avoid open-ended language in the order form that forces a procurement hold. Can your team share a brief note and suggested redline for the order form DPA clauses?

Prefer to have this by end of day Friday so procurement can clear the term sheet.

Thanks,
Anna Smith
Head of Legal Ops, DataMed Diagnostics

Anna — thanks for the specifics. Looping in Karthik (privacy counsel) and Ben (solutions/ops) to draft a concise response and an order-form redline.

Quick notes while we pull together the doc:
- The fallback path is operationally a region-to-region routing to our EU-dedicated pool (Frankfurt) with automatic KV cache purge; we can commit in the order form to that specific fallback region rather than generic "fallback to alternate hosting."
- For KMS/evidence: we can provide a scoped evidentiary checklist (export-controls-summary.xlsx) and commit to producing KMS key metadata and proof-of-processing on request under an agreed timeline.

We'll attach a suggested redline and the one-page mapping. Expect a follow-up in ~2 hours.

Best,

All — attaching two items: 1) a clean redline for the DPA/order form (DataMed_SLA_redlines_v2.docx) and 2) a 1-page export-controls summary (export-controls-summary.xlsx).

Summary of legal changes I propose (high-level):
- Replace the generic fallback language in Section 3.2 of the Order Form with: "Fallback hosting region: EU-FR (Frankfurt) for EU-covered accounts; Redwood will route processing to its EU-dedicated pool and execute KV cache purge within 1 hour of routing activation."
- Add an Exhibit B (Transfer evidence): commits to provide KMS key metadata, SCC flow diagram, and a list of subprocessors with hosting regions within 5 business days of request.
- Clarify that SCCs in Appendix A remain the primary legal mechanism; the fallback is strictly operational and not intended to change the legal transfer basis.

Operational/ops ask for Ben: confirm that the 1-hour purge and Frankfurt instance availability are feasible under Dedicated and Private deployment modes (we can scope for Hosted as best-effort).

If DataMed wants a hard SLA on purge time we should discuss procurement tradeoffs; otherwise propose the 1-hour operational commitment in the order form and a 30-day remediation SLA.

-Karthik

On Fri, Jul 18, 2025 at 09:42 AM Anna Smith <anna.smith@datamed.com> wrote:
> Laura/Karthik — quick follow up: is the 1-hour purge an absolute requirement for you, or can we accept a 4-hour window with an incident-based fallback?

Anna / team — operationally we can commit to the Frankfurt fallback and the purge. The 1-hour window is achievable for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we need the 4-hour window as the default because of batching and multi-tenant routing.

Proposed compromise to put in the order form:
- For Dedicated/Private: KV cache purge within 1 hour of routing activation;
- For Hosted: KV cache purge within 4 hours;
- For all: Redwood will provide KMS metadata and a transfer-evidence bundle within 5 business days.

If DataMed requires an absolute 1-hour SLA across all deployment modes, that triggers a technical add-on (Dedicated reserved capacity) and a pricing premium — happy to provide numbers.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
